## Assistant's notes (may be inaccurate)

Use these only for choices the user confirmed in the conversation that are missing from their request below. Never add a feature, database, framework, tool or deployment step that is not in the user's request; where these notes disagree with it, the user's request wins.

Update the existing web app dashboard incrementally. Fix Emergency cover so its number appears. Remove the EUR overview section from the dashboard, including This month income, This month expenses, This month total, Average monthly income, Average monthly expenses, and Average monthly total. Calculate “Left to spend this month” as this month's income minus this month's expenses. Add a right-aligned “About Pockindle” entry to the top menu linking to a page that explains the app's functionality and how to use it, names Mauro Dalle Lucca Tosi as the developer, and includes a “Built with BESSER” tag. Add the same tag and the year 2026 to the app footer.

## The user's original request, verbatim

This is the authority. Where the summary above is shorter or differs, this text wins.

I would like to create an app to manage my personal finance. I would like to be able to add my revenues, my fix, variable, and extraordinary expenses. Then, the app should be able to calculate my monthly cashflow indicating how much money I will have in my account in the end of the current and following months. 

The app should allow me to have multiple accounts entered in parallel. Consequently, I would like to able to check the cashflow in each account separately and in a set of accounts as well (as if they were a single account). Note, I would like to be able to decide which accounts to consolidate into a single view. 

I should be able to classify each revenue and expense by its category. 

The app should be visually pleasant and easy to use. 

I would also like to have a dashboard showing to me the most relevant information from my spendings on the current month, the ones to follow, and my averge spending.

This later request takes precedence where it changes earlier requirements.

I would like to update the app.

- Categories should not be mandatory. 
- I should be able to transfer money from one account to another one.
- In the dashboard, you can remove the main "Feel at home..." card. 
- In the dashboard, the "Following months’ spending" should actually be removed
- In the dashboard, there should be a widget with two pie charts showing the categories of the revenues and the expenses.
- The table in the dashboard should be colored based if I ended the month with positive or negative total in that month, and in general. 
- The user should be able to select which table to show in the dashboard, giving the options: individual accounts, groups, total
- Rename the app to "Pockindle"
- Currency code should come from a list including EUR, BRL, USD

## Subsequent user request, verbatim

This later request takes precedence where it changes earlier requirements.

I would like to update the dashboard withe the following:

1. Where am I now
Current balance (net worth). Total balance today across accounts, with the change since last month and a small trend line. Today the dashboard only shows future months, so the actual balance never appears.
Account balances. One line per account with today's balance and a 6-month trend line. It replaces the "pick an account" dropdown for a quick read.
This month so far. Income received vs expected, and expenses so far vs planned, as two progress bars. The key number is "Left to spend this month": expected income minus committed fixed costs minus what's already spent.
2. What needs attention
Missing amounts. Variable expenses and incomes for this month that still have no amount entered (needsActual in monthly.py already flags them). For example: "4 entries need this month's amount →". This keeps the data accurate, which every other widget depends on.
Coming up in the next 14 days. A short timeline of bills and income, with date, amount and account. It shows whether the right account will have money when a bill is due.
Low-balance warning. The first month an account (or group) is projected to drop below zero or below a threshold, e.g. "Checking goes to −120 EUR in March 2027". It can suggest a transfer, since you already support transfers. The cashflow table has this information, but users have to dig for it.
Off-plan entries. A compact version of the overages table: a count plus the worst case. It should also flag income below its expected minimum (expectedMinimum is already computed), not just expenses above the limit.
3. Where the money goes
Fixed vs variable vs extraordinary. A stacked bar plus the share of income already taken by fixed costs, e.g. "62% of your income is committed before the month starts." This is one of the best single measures of how much room a user has.
Category vs usual. Each category this month against its average over the last 3–6 months, with the difference ("Groceries +18%"). It shows changes better than pies, which only show proportions.
Recurring costs per year. Every recurring expense converted to a yearly cost (amount × 12 ÷ interval), sorted from largest. A line like "Subscriptions: 1,840 EUR/year" makes recurring costs visible, and spreading yearly bills into a monthly figure helps too.
Ending soon. Entries whose end date falls in the next few months, such as a loan paid off or a contract ending, e.g. "From May you'll have +250 EUR/month free."
4. The future
Balance forecast chart. A line chart of the projected end balance per month, with the lowest point marked ("Lowest: 340 EUR in Aug 2027"). It's much faster to read than the table. Keep the table as a detail view.
Savings rate trend. (Income − expenses) ÷ income per month, as a line, with a target line if you add goals later.
Big upcoming expenses. Large one-off or yearly expenses in the next 12 months, with how much to set aside each month to cover them.
Emergency cover. Current balance ÷ average monthly fixed expenses, e.g. "You could cover 4.2 months of fixed costs."
